name: Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary
tagline: Estuarine mangroves where winter migrants arrive — best birding Nov–Feb
summary: Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary is an estuarine wetland near Kozhikode where 60+ migratory species arrive in winter (roughly November–February). Boat rides and mangrove islets make it a top spot for…
description: Kadalundi Bird Sanctuary sits at the mouth of the Kadalundi River where it meets the Arabian Sea. The sanctuary is a cluster of small islands, mangroves and mudflats that support a rich mix of resident and wintering birds.

The site matters because it is a regular stopover for migratory birds that follow the Central Asian and other flyways. Every winter the estuary fills with waders, terns, gulls and waterfowl, attracting local birdwatchers and visiting naturalists.

Visitors get quiet estuary views, guided or community-run country-boat trips among the islets, good shorebird and gull-watching in low tide, and easy access from Kozhikode and the nearby railway stations and airport.
The sanctuary forms part of the Kadalundi–Vallikkunnu community reserve and is managed as an ecotourism resource with participation from local boat owners and forest/eco authorities.
highlights: Prime winter season: migratory birds arrive from November and peak through February.
Estuarine habitat — mangroves, mudflats and small islets ideal for waders and terns.
Community-run country-boat rides take you among islets for close views.
Easy half-day visit from Kozhikode; good early-morning birding and photography.

sections.heading: Background
body: Kadalundi is an estuarine wetland and part of the Kadalundi–Vallikkunnu community reserve. The mosaic of mangrove-fringed islets and mudflats provides feeding and roosting habitat for resident birds and more than 60 species of winter migrants recorded in the area.

The site has been promoted as an ecotourism destination by state agencies; local communities operate licensed country boats under community-reserve arrangements supervised by the relevant authorities.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Come early (first light to mid-morning) for the best bird activity. Expect waders (sandpipers, plovers), terns, gulls, herons and a variety of winter ducks and wagtails. Some rarer gulls and shorebirds are recorded seasonally — arrival and peak times vary by species.

Take a supervised country-boat trip to the mangrove islets (arranged locally or through ecotour operators). Walk short riverside stretches and mudflats at low tide for close views of feeding birds; bring binoculars, a field guide and a long lens if you photograph.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: winter — roughly November through February is the prime window for migratory arrivals and peak birdwatching, though some guides list migrants through April. Check recent local reports before you go.

How to reach: Kadalundi lies on the Kozhikode coast (about 20–25 km from central Kozhikode). Calicut International Airport (Karipur) is the nearest airport (about 20–25 km by road). The small Kadalundi / Vallikkunnu area is also reachable by local trains and road; taxis and local buses run from Kozhikode. Confirm local boat timings and any visitor rules before you travel.

latest.text: Travel guides listing India's winter birding hotspots name Kadalundi among the best; they reiterate November–February as the sanctuary's peak migratory season.
Kerala ecotourism/community-reserve programs continue to emphasise licensed community boat operations and safety standards for island/mangrove visits at Kadalundi.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November–February (prime winter migratory season; some migrants appear from November and stay into March–April).
visitorInfo.howToReach: By road: about 20–25 km from Kozhikode city; taxis and local buses connect Kozhikode and nearby towns. By air: Calicut International Airport (Karipur) is the nearest (around 20–25 km). By rail: local stations (Kadalundi/Vallikkunnu/Kozhikode) provide rail access — confirm local onward transport.
etiquette: Go at first light or late afternoon for best bird activity and calm water for photography.
Book or check community/forest department boat trips in advance; follow guide instructions and wear a life-jacket.
Wear neutral-coloured clothes, carry binoculars and mosquito repellent; avoid loud noises and do not disturb roosting/feeding birds.
Confirm entry rules, boat availability, and any small fees before you travel (local documents and plans sometimes list modest entry/visitor charges).
